name: San Francisco Bay wind-driven screw pumping
description: A wind-driven screw pump moved brine between evaporation ponds, supporting solar salt production.

impact.note: One salt works using long-known wind and screw pumping to move brine; a local variant with no known successors.

date.label: Approximately 1890
date.basis: The source reports the date for this scoped event or archaeological context.

events.statement: ASME labels the surviving Hayward screw-pump landmark as 1890 and describes its use in salt production.

evidence.supports: ASME labels the surviving Hayward screw-pump landmark as 1890 and describes its use in salt production.
The source attributes this contribution to andrew-oliver.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated case currently researched, not a claim of the capability’s original invention or global priority.

caveats: The date concerns the surviving late pump; the account does not establish its first day in service or the invention of the screw pump.

research.note: Independent review checked the ASME landmark heading and design attribution. The heading gives 1890 but does not establish a precise date of installation or first operation.
